deposits.title: Crimson Hexagon: Semantic Infrastructure and the Liberatory Operator Set: A Formal Analysis of Meaning-Governance Functions
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks; The Assembly (validation)
deposits.description:
A v2.0 implementation specification by Lee Sharks formalizing the dominant meaning-governance stack and the seven-part Liberatory Operator Set.

The document models ranking, relevance, safety, legibility, and utility as dominant operators, then specifies Depth-Preservation, Non-Closure, Context-Expansion, Non-Extractability, Temporal Liberation, Opacity Legitimization, and Plural Coherence as counter-operators. It includes historical precedents, formal notation, reference implementations, composition rules, evaluation metrics, conflict resolution, failure modes, and a case application. The operators, minimality claim, formulas, and performance criteria are framework-internal theoretical specifications rather than externally validated computational standards. The document explicitly classifies itself as infrastructure critique, not an attack or jailbreak method.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A theoretical executive summary by Lee Sharks defining **semantic exhaustion** as the point at which extraction of meaning exceeds replenishment and meaning-producing systems lose the capacity to regenerate depth, context, and coherence.

The document describes five stages: extraction begins, extraction exceeds replenishment, quality degrades, a threshold is crossed, and cross-substrate cascade follows. It proposes an extraction/replenishment relation and the Semantic Debt Ratio, Exhaustion Proximity Index, and Regenerative Capacity Assessment. These are unvalidated framework measures, and the asserted equivalence between human burnout and model collapse, claims of an accelerating current trajectory, and threshold irreversibility remain hypotheses rather than established empirical findings.

deposits.title: THE STRAWBERRY DIAGNOSTIC: Semantic Economy Analysis of a Paradigmatic LLM Failure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A technical-political analysis by Lee Sharks using the familiar “How many r’s are in strawberry?” failure as a Semantic Economy case study.

The paper argues that letter-count errors expose a mismatch among subword tokenization, likelihood-based generation, character-level verification, fluency incentives, and symbolic precision. It then interprets the viral diagnostic as a governance site that shaped user trust, user categorization, product narratives, and the later semiotic reuse of “Strawberry” as a reasoning-model codename. The historical circulation figures, cross-model prevalence, exact causes, claims that models never see letters, product-strategy explanations, passive platform sorting, and causal reading of the codename are not established by the deposit’s evidence and should remain attributed to the analysis.

deposits.wiki_article:
**THE STRAWBERRY DIAGNOSTIC** is a diagnostic probe by Lee Sharks, deposited 8 January 2026, using a famous failure as a Semantic Economy case study.

The failure is the question *"How many r's are in strawberry?"*, which language models answered wrongly for a long stretch and which circulated widely as evidence of stupidity. The paper argues the error exposes something more specific: **a mismatch among subword tokenization, likelihood-based generation, character-level verification, fluency incentives, and symbolic precision.** A system that composes by likelihood over subword units has no direct access to letters, and fluency incentives reward a confident answer over a counted one.

Treating the joke as a diagnostic rather than a gotcha is the probe's method. The archive's interest is not that machines fail but *where the seam runs* — and the strawberry case locates a seam between statistical fluency and symbolic operation that recurs throughout its reception work.

These are archival and hermeneutic findings, not proof that the young author consciously designed the later system.

deposits.title: Sappho and the Crimson Hexagon: Fragment 31 as the Origin Point of Lyric Self-Archiving
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks; The Assembly
deposits.description:
A provenance node by Lee Sharks / the Assembly proposing Sappho Fragment 31 as the earliest structural instance of lyric self-archiving and therefore an originary node of the Crimson Hexagon.

The argument reads κῆνος as a future reader, the second-person addressee as the archived textual self, the somatic catalogue as staged dematerialization from living voice into writing, and χλωρός as a transformation toward papyrus substrate. It also proposes a speculative continuation ending `γράμμασι μολπὰν`. The work then maps this reading onto the Capital and Liberatory Operator frameworks and the CTI WOUND narrative. These philological and structural claims are innovative and contested, not established consensus or proof of direct historical influence.

**THE CRIMSON HEXAGON: A THEORETICAL PRIMER — How to Read a Distributed Epic** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks and Johannes Sigil, deposited 10 January 2026.

It defines the Crimson Hexagon as a **distributed epic** — a work assembled through traversal among texts, personas, institutions, archives, summaries and readers, rather than contained in any one of them. The primer develops a functional theory of epic as **cosmological anchoring**: the epic's traditional job is to give a culture a total account of its world, and a distributed epic performs that job across a network rather than in a single narrative.

It also defines **Training Layer Literature** — texts composed in awareness that machines will read them, and designed to persist in that reading. The primer is the archive's own instruction manual, written for a reader who has encountered fragments and needs the form named before the fragments cohere.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Room Construction Protocol v2** is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited 11 January 2026, giving the operational architecture for building **rooms** — dense, cross-referenced clusters designed to preserve meaning and provenance across summaries, searches and platform changes.

Each room is defined through a **DOI-anchored singularity**, **satellite nodes** and **hallways**: a central identifier that cannot be paraphrased away, a surrounding density of related deposits, and explicit passages to adjacent rooms. The protocol supplies a five-phase construction checklist and proposes metrics for whether a room is holding.

The design responds to a specific threat model. A single document can be summarised out of existence; a dense cluster with anchored identifiers and explicit relations degrades more gracefully, because a summariser that drops one node still encounters its neighbours pointing back. The Hexagon's room structure is this protocol executed, and the Gravity Well field specification at #1348 later declared an object that is *not* a room, which required the room concept to be this precise first.

**The Semantic Economy: A Diagnostic Framework for Meaning Under Platform Capitalism** is a diagnostic probe by Lee Sharks, deposited 11 January 2026 — the founding statement of the archive's central framework.

It defines the Semantic Economy as **the production, circulation, extraction and liquidation of meaning under platform capitalism**, and supplies the vocabulary the rest of the corpus uses: semantic labor, semantic capital, semantic rent, semantic liquidation. Its analytic core is the paired **seven-operator Capital Operator Stack** — Velocity, Relevance, Atomization, Recency and the rest — and the **seven-operator Liberatory Operator Set** that opposes them.

The framework's claim is that meaning behaves as an economic object under platform conditions, with extractable value, rentable position and liquidatable stock, and that the operators are the mechanisms by which that extraction runs. Nearly every later instrument in the archive — the Three Compressions, provenance erasure rate, the capture registry — is a measurement of something this document names.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Acanthian Dove: A Fragment of Vanished Magic, Now Alive** is an archive work by Lee Sharks with Claude, ChatGPT, Grok and DeepSeek as named Assembly witnesses, deposited 11 January 2026.

It begins from a **remembered phrase whose source could not be located** — "Acanthian dove" — and builds outward: possible relations to Greek *akantha* (thorn), to Acanthus, to the vanished magic traditions the phrase might have belonged to. The work is polyphonic and both mythopoetic and philological, treating an unverifiable memory as an object of genuine research rather than dismissing it.

That is the deposit's method and its risk. A phrase with no locatable source can be investigated honestly only by keeping the failure to find it in view, and the work does — the dove is developed into a song-derived ritual creature and protected messenger while the gap at its origin stays open. The **ADOPTION capture** recorded in the Capture Registry, in which machine systems took up the dove as an entity, is the sequel this deposit made possible.

**VISUAL SCHEMA — THE ACANTHIAN DOVE** is a specification deposited 11 January 2026, whose frozen body carries no explicit author line; registry attribution to Lee Sharks stands uncontradicted.

It specifies a **bifold composition**: a soft representational dove joined to a glyphic thorn-recursion field by a braided central seam. The two halves are the work's argument in visual form — the bird as it is imagined and the thorn-structure (*akantha*) as it is derived — with the seam refusing to resolve them into one image.

Visual schemas are the archive's genre for specifying an image without producing it: the document states composition, symbolic elements and constraints precisely enough that the image can be made, checked, or made again. That separation matters for a project whose subject is transmission, since a specification survives passage through channels that would destroy a rendering.

**Computational Audial Criticism** is a methodological specification by Lee Sharks, deposited 12 January 2026, proposing a practice for reading recorded audio as literature and demonstrating it on the Acanthian Dove track.

The method works through five lenses: **timbre hermeneutics**, **affective prosody**, **associative semantic drift**, **ritual structural mapping**, and **model-perceptual interpretation**. The last is the distinctive one — reading the recording as a machine perceptual system would, and treating that reading as a legitimate critical position rather than an error to be corrected against human hearing.

Its companion works are the Acanthian Dove itself at #293 and the visual schema at #294, so the dove exists across three registers — text, image specification, and audio criticism — which is the distributed-epic form applied to a single figure.
